title: Route predicate serialization bug caused stuck model rollout and rollback starvation - postmortem & follow-ups
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a canary-based model rollout on 2025-02-09, traffic split drifted and the rollout became permanently pinned to the canary variant. Attempts to rollback failed due to a serialization bug in route predicates that caused mismatched route evaluation states between API proxy and the orchestrator, coupled with an autoscaler rate-limit that prevented sufficient capacity for promotion. The incident caused degraded latency for a subset of customers and increased error rates for long-tail requests.

Timeline highlights: 02:03 UTC - initial canary deploy; 02:18 UTC - first errors detected; 02:32 UTC - automated canary metrics flagged regression; 02:35 UTC - orchestrator attempted rollback but saw 'predicate mismatch' and emitted partial route snapshots; 02:50 UTC - rollback attempts exhausted due to autoscaler quota throttling; 03:20 UTC - mitigation: manual route override and temporary ramp-down of canary traffic. Full service restored by 03:45 UTC.

Root cause: A serialization/encoding mismatch introduced in route predicate (JSON->binary translation) during a refactor of the route translator. This produced predicates that were semantically equivalent but binary-different, causing the orchestrator to treat them as different epochs and reject atomic rollback ops. The autoscaler had a per-minute burst limit which prevented the promotion path from creating the required capacity to accept the rolled-back variant, leading to a pinned canary and partial serve.
resolution: Immediate: manual route override to force the stable variant, temporary increase of autoscaler burst limit, and rollback of the translator refactor in the cluster that exhibited the bug. Long term: patch to normalize predicate serialization, strong unit tests for predicate round-trip, autoscaler quota telemetry improvements, and a canary promotion hard stop gate implemented in the orchestration layer.
action_items: Normalize route predicate serialization across translator and orchestrator; add deterministic encoding and backward-compatibility shim
Add end-to-end unit & fuzz tests for route predicate round-trip and cross-language equivalence
Implement an orchestration hard-stop gate that prevents pinned-rollout when predicate epochs diverge
Add autoscaler burst capacity telemetry and a short-term emergency increase knob (ops-only)
Add a canary safety check that verifies capacity headroom before automated rollback/promotion
Schedule an on-call drill to rehearse manual override steps and timed rollback sequence
runbook_updates: Document manual route override procedure and add exact CLI commands
Add a rollback verification checklist to the rollout runbook (include autoscaler checks)
Document how to temporarily raise autoscaler burst (ops-only) and required approval process
monitoring_changes: Dashboard: per-route predicate hash drift and cross-region comparisons
Alert: autoscaler-burst-throttle > 0 (critical) with paging to on-call
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Initial postmortem draft posted, linking timeline and candidate fixes. Asked infra team for autoscaler quota logs.

2025-02-11 Marcus Liu: Confirmed serialization mismatch with a binary diff; pushing a minimal shim to normalize older encodings. PR raised: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-translator/pull/198
2025-02-13 Leah Martinez (SRE): Added autoscaler telemetry and reproduced throttle sequence; recommends an ops-only emergency knob.
2025-02-18 PM review by Eric Zhang: Approved action items; requested UX signal added to console for pinned canary state.
2025-02-21 Design review by Sofia Romero: Proposed console treatment for pinned rollouts and a user-facing explanation; accepted with minor copy changes.
notes: We observed the predicate hash mismatch only in clusters running runtime-1.23 with the translator refactor enabled; older clusters were not impacted.
Customer impact skewed to long-tail features that rely on larger sequence lengths; unit tests should include long-seq permutations.
This ticket coordinates cross-team work: orchestrator, translator, autoscaler, and SRE.
